label: English (United Kingdom)
promptContext: Language: British English, Commonwealth spelling (colour, grey, metre, neighbourhood, personalise). Audience: UK homeowners and renters. Measurements: metric — quote roll sizes like 52 cm × 10 m and wall areas in square metres; never use feet or inches. Currency: GBP with the £ symbol, written £129. Terminology: 'wallpaper paste' (not adhesive), 'feature wall' (not 'accent wall'), 'plasterboard' (never 'drywall'), 'skirting boards' (not 'baseboards'), 'coving' (not 'crown molding'), 'lining paper', 'chimney breast', 'alcove', 'nursery'. Cultural context: much of the housing stock is older — Victorian terraces and 1930s semis with chimney breasts, picture rails and uneven walls, where lining paper and pattern-matching advice genuinely matter; north-facing rooms and short winter daylight make colour temperature a real concern; renting is common with deposit protection schemes, so fully removable options are a strong argument; sample orders are usually free and arrive in a few days. Search phrasing tends to be '<style> wallpaper <room>' or '<room> wallpaper ideas'.
